title: Subscription cursors with CURSOR_GAP snapshots
description: Objective: let a consumer follow projection output from a durable cursor, and detect when it has fallen too far behind to resume incrementally. SPIDR step 4 of 5, split from task-55d5a898264b4880a99bf2c5b3be120b. Deliverable: subscription registration with durable cursors keyed to the cursor-generation table from step 1, bounded page reads over projection output, and a stable CURSOR_GAP outcome when a cursor is older than retained history — accompanied by a snapshot the consumer can rebuild from, so CURSOR_GAP is a recoverable answer rather than a dead end. A reopened subscription whose generation has changed reports the gap rather than silently resuming against incompatible state. NOT in scope: the relay/inbox transaction, the projection fold itself, crash/rebuild hardening drills. Hard dependencies: Versioned event schema and projection commit seam (step 1) for the subscription and cursor-generation tables; Transactional outbox relay with durable inbox dedupe (step 3) for the projection output being followed. Owned paths: packages/store/src/subscriptions/** and its focused tests. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/store typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/store test.
definitionOfDone: Subscription cursors are durable across restart and bound to a cursor generation; a reopened subscription whose generation changed reports CURSOR_GAP rather than resuming against incompatible state.
A cursor older than retained history returns a stable CURSOR_GAP outcome together with a snapshot sufficient to rebuild from, never a silent skip and never an unbounded replay.
Page reads are bounded and deterministic: the same cursor returns the same frozen page, and cursor ordering is total with no duplicate or skipped entries at page boundaries.
The focused store typecheck and test command exits 0 and only explicitly owned paths are staged and committed.
taskRails: CURSOR_GAP must be recoverable. Reporting the gap without a usable snapshot leaves the consumer stuck and fails this task.
Never silently skip ahead to close a gap. A missed range is a stable reason code, not a repositioned cursor.
Consume the relay's output; do not reach into packages/store/src/outbox-relay/** or projections/** to reshape it. Raise contract problems in #architects instead.
Page reads must be bounded — no unbounded replay of retained history.
Use TDD. Keep each production source focused, target <=250 lines, split before 400. Commit by explicit pathspec only.

implementationPlan.description: PHASE 1+2+3 (contracts + doc codec, TDD). Write subscription-docs.test.ts RED first, then subscription-contracts.ts + one-line .js bridge (`export * from "./subscription-contracts.ts";` — package convention: every production non-entrypoint .ts gets one; test files do not). CONTENT: (1) Doc versions `moe-subscription/1` (subscriber doc: {version, projection, filter, cursor:{generation:number, position:decimal-string}, receiptDigest}) and `moe-subscription-snapshot/1` (snapshot doc: {version, projection, generation, checkpoint:decimal-string, state:DataRecord, stateDigest, receiptDigest}); reserved sentinel prefix constant `moe-snapshot/` (sentinel subscriber_id = `moe-snapshot/<projectionName>`; requireIdentifier from store-input-primitives.ts has NO charset whitelist so slashes pass — enforce the prefix refusal yourself). (2) Closed unions: layers `INPUT|STATE|SOURCE`; codes `SUBSCRIPTION_INPUT_INVALID | SUBSCRIPTION_NOT_REGISTERED | SUBSCRIPTION_GENERATION_MISSING | SUBSCRIPTION_GENERATION_BASELINE_MISSING | SUBSCRIPTION_CURSOR_REGRESSION | SUBSCRIPTION_SNAPSHOT_REGRESSION | SUBSCRIPTION_SNAPSHOT_STALE | SUBSCRIPTION_STATE_CORRUPT | SUBSCRIPTION_STORE_BUSY`; gap causes `GENERATION_CHANGED|HISTORY_PRUNED|CURSOR_CORRUPT|CURSOR_AHEAD`. (3) Result unions mirroring outbox-relay-contracts.ts style — payload fields live ONLY on the owning arm: PAGE {outcome, events, nextCursor, hasMore, checkpoint}, CURSOR_GAP {outcome, cause, lastGoodCursor: cursor|null, snapshot}, REFUSED {outcome, code, layer, detail}. (4) LOCAL structural types only — SnapshotPublishInput {checkpoint: bigint, state, stateDigest, projection, generation}, event-source seam {readEventsAfter(after: bigint, limit?: number, maxDecodedBytes?: number): CursorPage<StoredEvent,bigint>} — ZERO imports from outbox-relay/** or projections/** (type-only imports are still imports; the rail bans them; SqliteEventStore satisfies the seam structurally). Allowed imports: store-contracts.js, store-rows.js, store-input-primitives.js, read-page-budget.js, sqlite-schema-bootstrap.js (isSqliteBusy), store-internals.js. (5) Doc codec: canonical serialize (sorted keys, stable) + sha256 receiptDigest via node:crypto — there is NO reusable canonical-digest helper outside outbox-relay/** (verified: store-digests.ts framing helpers are module-private), so implement a small domain-separated, length-framed digest following the store-digests.ts pattern; hash the EXACT canonical text you store (never re-encode parsed output — lone surrogates collapse under TextEncoder and would let two distinct stored docs share a digest); one strict parsePosition helper (regex ^0$|^[1-9]\d*$ then BigInt) used by EVERY position comparison. TESTS (assert exact code + layer per epic rail 6): codec round-trip; key-order-independent digest (same content, different insertion order → SAME digest); framing collision pair (shifting a char between two adjacent framed fields → DIFFERENT digest); tamper matrix '007', '1e3', '-1', empty string, lone surrogate → refused/CURSOR_CORRUPT-bound; oversized doc refused SUBSCRIPTION_INPUT_INVALID.

implementationPlan.description: PHASE 3 (writes TDD, RED). Write subscription-writes.test.ts against the not-yet-written subscription-writes.ts API. Test setup pattern (canonical precedent: withStore in transactional-outbox-relay.test.ts:96-102): mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(),...)) + SqliteEventStore.openForProject(path, projectId) — NOT SqliteEventStore.open(path), which passes requestedProjectId=null and cannot commit (PROJECT_SCOPE_REQUIRED); :memory: stores are per-connection and unusable here. Module state connection: second `new DatabaseSync(path, {timeout: 5000})` — WAL is a persistent DB property (no journal pragma needed), node:sqlite enables FK by default, but the default busy timeout is 0 so the timeout option is REQUIRED or a BEGIN IMMEDIATE colliding with the store writer fails instantly. COVER (assert exact code + layer): (a) registerSubscription refuses when cursor_generations is empty → SUBSCRIPTION_GENERATION_MISSING; refuses reserved-prefix subscriber ids → SUBSCRIPTION_INPUT_INVALID (and so does EVERY other entry point — acknowledge, reseatToSnapshot, readSubscriptionPage — a reseat aimed at a sentinel id would overwrite the baseline snapshot and kill recoverability; after each refused call assert the sentinel row bytes are UNCHANGED); duplicate registration refused; success seats cursor at snapshot.checkpoint (default) and returns the snapshot; ORIGIN start mode allowed only when (floor exists AND floor <= 1) OR (ledger empty AND checkpoint == 0). (b) advanceGeneration REQUIRES a baseline snapshot per covered projection: it must refuse SUBSCRIPTION_GENERATION_BASELINE_MISSING unless baselines are supplied for every projection that currently has a snapshot sentinel OR a live subscriber doc (two-projection fixture: advance with one baseline → refused; with both → both recover). Sentinel write must be an UPSERT (subscriber_id is PK — a second advance for the same projection would otherwise PK-conflict); generation numbering max+1 starting at 1; generation row + all baseline sentinels land in ONE BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction. (c) publishSnapshot CAS: checkpoint regression → SUBSCRIPTION_SNAPSHOT_REGRESSION; stale generation → refused (the CAS predicate must match BOTH stored generation AND stored checkpoint, mirroring the relay's PROJECTION_UPSERT double predicate — test the race by mutating cursor_generations via raw SQL between building the publish input and calling publishSnapshot). (d) acknowledge CAS: backward → SUBSCRIPTION_CURSOR_REGRESSION; beyond projection checkpoint → SUBSCRIPTION_INPUT_INVALID; generation mismatch refused; success durable — close store + module connection, reopen both, cursor reads back exactly (DoD 1). (e) reseatToSnapshot: only sanctioned reseat, takes NO position argument, seats cursor at current snapshot generation+checkpoint and returns the snapshot; REFUSES SUBSCRIPTION_SNAPSHOT_STALE (layer STATE) when snapshot.checkpoint + 1 < retained floor — otherwise reseat/gap livelocks when history was pruned past the snapshot. (f) SQLITE_BUSY (via isSqliteBusy) → SUBSCRIPTION_STORE_BUSY. Suite must be RED for the right reason (module missing), not import-crashed.

implementationPlan.description: PHASE 3 (read-page TDD, RED). Write subscription-read-page.test.ts. GAP MATRIX (each asserts outcome CURSOR_GAP + exact cause + snapshot content deep-equal + lastGoodCursor): (1) GENERATION_CHANGED — advanceGeneration then read with old-generation cursor; snapshot must be the NEW generation's baseline; then reseatToSnapshot + re-read resumes cleanly from snapshot.checkpoint (recovery loop closes — DoD 1+2). (2) HISTORY_PRUNED — simulate pruning on the OPEN store handle via second connection: DELETE only PREFIX (non-tail) domain_events rows of an aggregate, from commands the test never re-reads via getCommandReceipt/replay (assertAggregateTail in store-runtime.ts:119-156 fires on every commit and getAggregateVersion and only checks the TAIL, so prefix deletion is invisible to it; commits with zero outbox drafts are legal so rows are FK-deletable; the DB is UNREOPENABLE afterwards — min(global_position)=1 and sqlite_sequence checks fail at open — finish the case on the open handle and discard the tempdir). Cursor with position+1 < min(global_position) → HISTORY_PRUNED, never a silently repositioned cursor, never an empty-page stall. (3) Empty-ledger NULL-floor branch BOTH ways: DELETE ALL rows with projection checkpoint > cursor.position → HISTORY_PRUNED (min() is NULL — an unguarded SQL comparison is falsy and would silently stall; branch explicitly); fresh store, checkpoint == 0, cursor 0 → empty PAGE, hasMore false, NOT a gap. (4) CURSOR_CORRUPT — tamper subscriber filter_json via raw SQL (bad digest, '007' position, wrong version): gap with lastGoodCursor null but snapshot still carried (recoverable); corrupt or MISSING snapshot sentinel instead → REFUSED SUBSCRIPTION_STATE_CORRUPT layer STATE (never a fabricated snapshot). (5) CURSOR_AHEAD — cursor.position > checkpoint (gap-with-snapshot, deliberately not a refusal: reseat is the sanctioned repositioning). PAGE SEMANTICS: clamp to global_position <= checkpoint — event EXACTLY at checkpoint included, first event beyond excluded, hasMore/nextCursor recomputed within the clamped bound (readEventsAfter sees the whole ledger; hasMore must reflect remaining events <= checkpoint only); cursor == checkpoint → empty PAGE not gap. DETERMINISM (DoD 3): same cursor+checkpoint → deep-equal page across repeated reads AND after appending events beyond the checkpoint; full pagination sweep at page sizes {1, 3, exact-multiple, larger-than-remaining} concatenates to exactly positions 1..N with no duplicate or skip at any boundary — the sweep must assert its own generated case count > 0 (epic rail: a sweep that generates zero cases passes while testing nothing). SEAM ERRORS: a stub event source throwing DurableStoreError (STORE_BUSY, STORE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED) → rethrown VERBATIM, not translated (relay's rule: uncertainty keeps its authority). FREEZE: returned page and event objects frozen WITHOUT freezing Uint8Array payload/metadata (Object.freeze on a non-empty TypedArray THROWS TypeError — skip ArrayBuffer views, like the relay's materializer); one test proves a page with a non-empty payload returns frozen wrappers without throwing.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Durable cursor home: (a) v4 schema migration adding cursor columns — rejected: touches manifest/migration/internals outside owned paths and the migration path refuses populated stores; (b) store_metadata keys — impossible, validateSchemaManifestMetadata pins the table to EXACTLY one row (sqlite-schema-conformance.ts:55-72); (c) HUMAN-APPROVED: versioned JSON docs in event_subscriptions.filter_json, snapshots as sentinel rows under reserved prefix moe-snapshot/<projection>. New tables are impossible: validateExactSchemaObjects rejects ANY unlisted object on EVERY open. Snapshot provenance: caller publishes relay APPLIED results via publishSnapshot; module never folds events itself (unbounded replay rail) and never fabricates snapshots. Recoverability is BY CONSTRUCTION: advanceGeneration refuses unless baselines cover every projection with a sentinel or live subscriber (single-baseline design was a verified BLOCKER: other projections' subscribers would loop reseat→gap forever). Canonical digest: NO reusable helper exists outside outbox-relay/** (verified — store-digests framing helpers are module-private, decision-ledger-canonical has no hashing), so the module implements its own length-framed domain-separated sha256; extraction of the relay's encoder was rejected as an out-of-owned-paths refactor.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: readEventsAfter(afterGlobalPosition: bigint, limit=100, maxDecodedBytes?): CursorPage<StoredEvent,bigint> at sqlite-event-store.ts:312; StoredEvent.globalPosition is bigint (store-contracts.ts:167), payload/metadata are Uint8Array — Object.freeze on a non-empty TypedArray THROWS, freeze wrappers only. CursorPage = {hasMore, items, nextCursor} (store-contracts.ts:186-190). Bridge convention: every production non-entrypoint .ts has a one-line `export * from "./<name>.ts";` sibling .js; index.ts and *-test-helpers.ts are the only exceptions. File-backed committing tests: mkdtempSync + openForProject (open() cannot commit — PROJECT_SCOPE_REQUIRED). Second DatabaseSync on the same file while the store is open is established test practice (transactional-outbox-relay.test.ts:108-135); it MUST set {timeout: 5000} (node:sqlite default busy timeout is 0). Integrity checks are OPEN-time only, but assertAggregateTail runs on every commit/getAggregateVersion and checks the TAIL — prune only aggregate PREFIXES, never re-read pruned commands' receipts, never reopen the pruned DB. requireIdentifier has no charset whitelist (slash ok, 512-byte cap). CURSOR_GAP and SUBSCRIPTION_* literals collide with nothing (scheduler's SUBSCRIPTION_QUOTA is a different domain — don't reuse that exact token). Relay result-union style: payload fields only on the owning arm (answer to mem:gotcha-union-refusal-echo-unnarrowed).
planningNotes.risks: (1) Reserved-prefix guard must live in a SHARED validator on every entry point — reseatToSnapshot aimed at a sentinel id would overwrite the baseline and destroy recoverability. (2) All CAS predicates need generation AND checkpoint, with every dependent read inside the same BEGIN IMMEDIATE — a checkpoint-only CAS lets a stale-generation publishSnapshot clobber the new baseline in a plain two-writer race. (3) Empty domain_events makes min() NULL — an unguarded comparison silently stalls instead of reporting HISTORY_PRUNED; branch explicitly both ways. (4) reseatToSnapshot must refuse SUBSCRIPTION_SNAPSHOT_STALE when snapshot.checkpoint+1 < floor, else pruned-past-snapshot livelocks. (5) Positions are decimal TEXT — every comparison goes through one strict parsePosition ('9'>'10' lexicographically; '007'/'1e3' from tampered docs must land in CURSOR_CORRUPT, not coerce). (6) Digest must hash the exact stored canonical text (lone surrogates collapse under TextEncoder re-encoding). (7) Zero imports from outbox-relay/** or projections/** including type-only — use local structural types; QA will grep. (8) File budget: 3 prod + 3 bridges + 3 tests = 9 of 10 hard cap; one slack slot — if subscription-writes.ts bursts 400 lines, amend_plan_step to split reseat/advance out. (9) Prune-simulation DBs are unreopenable — finish assertions on the open handle, discard the tempdir.
